Isabel Infantes | Reuters Shares of Pop Mart fell over 4% in Hong Kong on Friday after the Labubu maker reported first-half results that showed declining sales in Asia-Pacific and the Americas. For the period ended in June 30, the toy maker reported a 23.8% year-over-year rise in first-half revenue to 17.17 billion yuan ($2.55 billion). The company has faced challenges globally ranging from inventory management, supply chains to warehousing and logistics and store operation, according to Citi. Citi said management now sees its initial 20% revenue growth target for 2026 as difficult to achieve, given more challenges than expected and competitive pressure.
